spec_match.rationale: Classifies fetch targets into public/private/loopback/undecidable using the LNA address-space rules, including the RFC1918 boundaries (172.16/12 vs 172.32), .local names, and the DNS-undecidable case the spec makes central.

interactive.rationale: Editable URL list with audit button, tally counters and a per-URL verdict table; verified the default nine URLs produce 1 public / 3 private / 1 loopback / 4 undecidable with correct reasons.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises per-target permission requirements including undecidable-until-resolve entries, which the page delivers.

edge_cases.rationale: The 172.31-vs-172.32 boundary, link-local, .local mDNS names and hostname-undecidability are all in the default set; the all-or-nothing registration advice covers the failure mode.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6225598451154944 and the Local Network Access specification.

conformance.rationale: The suite honestly fails its two pre-154 permission assertions on this build; its background-fetch-requires-user-activation assertion fails for fresh-profile state reasons — flagged for a human, not edited.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): audit auto-ran and re-ran on click with correct classifications and tally (console: audited 9 {public:1,local:3,loopback:1,unknown:4}); console clean, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and logs the tally per audit.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, tally uses dl semantics, captioned table, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled textarea, captioned table with scoped headers, aria-live detail, 44px button.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read).

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/local-network-access-restrictions-for-background-fetch/target-audit/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). The classifier is precise where it matters — it gets the 172.16/12 boundary right, treats hostnames as undecidable until DNS answers rather than guessing, and pairs the audit with practical split-your-registrations advice. Verified the default list's tally and per-row reasons; console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; no overflow at 360. /conformance/ ran 4 pass / 3 fail — two honest pre-154 permission fails plus the fresh-profile user-activation assertion flagged at feature level. Clears the bar.
